chapter: New Orleans bands, Louis and the Lyric
title: Zutty's love of the theater and segregated seating in St. Louis
summary: Marge says Zutty always loved theaters and took her to shows in St. Louis, while she was bitter at having to sit upstairs. Dance praises his attitude.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: He always had that theater in his blood.

And I know that because when Zutty came and we started going together in St. Louis, I never thought about theater. I just wanted to ball & all my life. But Zutty wanted to go to the theater. He started me to going to the theater. He was always interested, not only in orchestras in Lin shows, but integrated. the theaters. And at that time it was not/many. We always had to sit upstairs. And I guess that's one thing that disgusted me at the theater in St. Louis. That Zutty started me on his night off to some show, it was a musical show or something. He'd get tickets for us to go to the theater. And I told him, I don't like to go. So Zutty said, well I do. I like to go to the
theater. And he was always, always watching the band and the drummer and everything. Loved the theater a lot. Started me liking it.

It's a very, you know, it's a very, shows a very nice trait in his character that he could you know, I mean, so as you say that the damn place was segregated and everything and yet he could see the virtue or the beauty in that regardless. Where, you know, you might feel very bitter and amgry and disgusted.

Well I did because I just, I know when we came up in St. Louis and East St. Louis you know, the segregation being and all that, I was just bitter. I didn't care anything about going to any shows, you had to go upstairs.
